$comment: Single source of truth for the Datastar 1.0.5 surface Streamlord knows: attributes, modifiers, actions, fetch options. streamlord-core compiles its names in (CatalogNames), streamlord-analysis compiles it in as text, the VS Code extension bundles it, and streamlord-html-pro/CatalogTest binds it to the DSL. Pro entries name only publicly documented attribute names; no Datastar Pro code is included anywhere.

modifierTypes.duration: a duration such as 500ms or 1s, e.g. __debounce.500ms, optionally followed by flags
modifierTypes.enum: one of the listed values, e.g. __case.kebab

case.name: case
case.doc: Converts the casing of the key.

viewtransition.doc: Wraps the expression in document.startViewTransition() when the View Transition API is available.

actions.name: setAll
parameterDocs: The value every matching signal is set to.
include picks the signals whose path it matches and exclude leaves out those it matches, each a regular expression or a string. Left out, it picks every signal.

actions.name: toggleAll
parameterDocs: include picks the signals whose path it matches and exclude leaves out those it matches, each a regular expression or a string. Left out, it picks every signal.

actions.name: peek
parameterDocs: Its signals are read without subscribing to them; @peek gives what it returns.

actions.name: clipboard
parameterDocs: The text to copy.
true when text is Base64, which is decoded before it is copied.
actions.doc: Pro. Copies text to the clipboard.

actions.name: fit
actions.signature: @fit(v, oldMin, oldMax, newMin, newMax, shouldClamp?, shouldRound?)
parameterDocs: The number to map from the old range to the new one.
The value of v that maps to newMin.
The value of v that maps to newMax.
What oldMin maps to.
What oldMax maps to.
true keeps the result within the new range; false when left out.
true rounds the result to the nearest whole number; false when left out.

actions.name: intl
parameterDocs: Which Intl formatter: datetime, number, pluralRules, relativeTime, list or displayNames.
The value to format.
The options of that formatter, as its Intl constructor takes them.
A locale or a list of them; the browser's when left out.

fetchOptions.name: contentType
fetchOptions.otherwise: Datastar throws FetchInvalidContentType and sends nothing
fetchOptions.doc: 'json' sends the signals as JSON: the body, or ?datastar= on the URL for @get and @delete. 'form' sends a form instead, the closest one or the one selector names, after the browser has validated it.

fetchOptions.name: filterSignals
fetchOptions.doc: Which signals a 'json' request sends: include and exclude are regular expressions matched against each signal's path. The default sends every signal except those whose name, at any level, starts with _ (_draft, user._token).

fetchOptions.name: selector
fetchOptions.doc: With contentType 'form', the CSS selector of the form to send in place of the closest one. A 'json' request does not read it.

fetchOptions.name: headers
fetchOptions.doc: Headers added to the request, after Datastar's own Accept and Datastar-Request: true.

fetchOptions.name: openWhenHidden
fetchOptions.doc: Whether the request stays open while the tab is hidden. When false, Datastar closes it as the tab is hidden and sends it again as the tab is shown.

fetchOptions.name: payload
fetchOptions.doc: What a 'json' request sends in place of the signals; filterSignals is then not read.

fetchOptions.name: requestCancellation
fetchOptions.otherwise: Datastar cancels no other request, as with 'disabled'
fetchOptions.doc: 'auto' cancels a request with the same method and URL that is still running; 'cleanup' does so too, and also cancels the request when its element or attribute goes; 'disabled' lets requests run side by side. An AbortController cancels the request from your own code.

fetchOptions.name: retry
fetchOptions.doc: When Datastar sends the request again. 'auto' retries a request that fails on the network, before or during the response; 'error' also retries a 4xx or 5xx answer; 'always' also retries any status but 200, 204 or a redirect, and an event stream when it ends; 'never' retries nothing, and the action fails with the first error. A 200 answer of HTML, JSON or JavaScript is never retried.

fetchOptions.name: retryInterval
fetchOptions.otherwise: it waits no time before a retry
fetchOptions.doc: Milliseconds before the first retry, multiplied by retryScaler for each one after, and set back when an event stream has ended. A retry: line in the stream sets it too.

fetchOptions.name: retryScaler
fetchOptions.otherwise: every retry after the first comes at once
fetchOptions.doc: What the wait is multiplied by after each retry, up to retryMaxWait.

fetchOptions.name: retryMaxWait
fetchOptions.otherwise: every retry after the first comes at once
fetchOptions.doc: The longest the wait grows to as retryScaler multiplies it, in milliseconds. The first wait, retryInterval, and one a retry: line in the stream sets, are not held to it.

fetchOptions.name: retryMaxCount
fetchOptions.otherwise: it makes no retry at all
fetchOptions.doc: How many retries Datastar makes over the whole action before it gives up and dispatches retries-failed. An answer that arrives in between does not give it more.

datastarEvents.name: datastar-fetch
datastarEvents.doc: Dispatched on the document at each step of a backend action's request; data-on listens there on its own. evt.detail.type is started, finished, error, retrying, retries-failed or the datastar-* event the response sent, and evt.detail.el the element that sent the request.

datastarEvents.name: datastar-signal-patch
datastarEvents.doc: Dispatched on the document when signals change; data-on listens there on its own. evt.detail is the patch: the signals that changed, with their new values.

kotlinCallSites.$comment: Which Streamlord DSL functions take Datastar strings, and at which argument; an expression may also be passed by its parameter's name. more: the parameters after it that take an expression too, each by its place or its name. Used by the editor to know where to validate and complete.

expressionOptions.$comment: The options of FetchOptions whose value is an expression, set in the options' lambda: name = "...". map: the option is a map, headerExprs = mapOf("name" to "..."), whose values are the expressions.

signals.$comment: The calls whose arguments are signals by name, as pairs or names. names: the pair keys are signal names written in code, which a $ then reads. json: the call also takes the signals as JSON text.

signalNames.$comment: The expression helpers, whose first argument is a signal name written as JavaScript. reads: the helper reads the signal. shared: other APIs use the name in the same scope, so a call counts only inside a DSL call.
